Normal bats: These very small mammals weigh only a few ounces. They will not attack men but may _confuse_ them by Aying around their heads. There must be at least ten bats to _confuse_ one character. Characters who arc _confused_ have a - 2 penalty on their attack rolls and saving throws and cannot cast spells. Normal bats must check morale each round unless they arc controlled or summoned. 

_Monsrcr Type::_ Black, G rizzly Bears: Normal Animal (Common). Polar Bear: Normal Animal (Rare). Cave Bear: Prehistoric Animal (Very Rare). 

Bears are well known to all adventurers. lf any bear hits one vicdm with both paws in one round, the bear hugs its victim and inAicts 2d8 points of additional damage in that same round. 

Giant Bats: Giant bats are much larger cousins of normal bat species. Giant bats look like smaller bat species but grow to be approximately 5' long, with a wingspan greater than 25'. They are carnivores (or, more appropriately, hcmovores-blood-drinkers) and may attack humans if extremely hungry. 

Black Bear: Black bears have black fur and stand about 6' tall. They arc omnivores but prefer roots and berries. A black bear will not usually attack un less it is cornered and cannot escape. Adult black bears will fight to the death to protect their young. They have been known to raid camps, seeking food. They are especially fond of such treats as fresh fish and sweets. 

Giant Vampire Bats: Of giant bat encounters, 5% will be with groups of giant vampire bats, far more dangerous creatures (HD 2*, XP Value 25). The bite of a giant vampire bat docs no extra damage but its victim must make a saving throw vs. paralysis or fall unconscious for ld 10 rounds. This will allow t he vampire bat to feed without being disturbed, draining ld4 points of blood per round . Any victims who die from having their blood drained by a giant vampire bat musr make a saving throw vs. spells or become an undead creature _24_ hours after death. 

Grizzly Bear: Grizzly bears have silver-tipped brown or reddish brown fu r and stand about 9' tall. They arc fond of meat and are much more likely to attack than black bears. Grizzlies arc found in most climates, but arc most common in mountains and forests. 

Polar Bear: Polar bears have white fur and stand about 11 ' tall. They live in cold regions. They usually eat fish, but often attack adventurers. These huge bears are good swimmers, and their wide feet allow them to run across snow without sinking. 

_Tcrrain:_ Cavern, Ruins. 

_Load:_ Giant Bat: ~00 en at fu ll speed: 1.000 en at half speed. 

Cave Bear: These enormous bears stand about I 5' tall. They do not sec well at all but hunt very well by scent. If hungry, they will follow a track of blood until they have eaten. They prefer a diet of fresh-killed red m eat and live in caves, mostly in prehistoric envi.ronmcnrs or very distant mountain areas where human civilization has not penetrated . 

_Barding Multiplier:_ x I (Giant Bat). 

_Tcrrain:_ Hill, Mountain, Woods. (Cave Bear: Same, but prehistoric.)

_Monster Type:_ Planar Monster (Very Rare). It is not known what these curious beings are, or even if they are living creatures. A blackball (or "deadly sphere") is simply a featureless black globe, 5' in diameter. It moves slowly but usually randomly. Whatever it touches simply disintegrates (no saving throw), so it moves freely through anything. 

_Monster Type:_ Monster (Common). _This_ unusual creature is a small, brown-furred, rugged-looking cartine with big jaws. It is not, however, a normal animal. It is intelligent, often travels in packs, and uses a limited teleponarion ability. It can "blink out" of one spot and immediately appear ("blink in") at another. It has inscincts that prevent it from appearing in a solid object. 

_Monster Type:_ Humanoid (Common). Bugbears are giant hairy goblins-humanoids that grow to about 8' rail and are covered with bristly dark fur. 

When encountered, the blackball moves toward the nearest intelligent creature within 60'. It has no recognizable mind or intelligence and _is_ immune to everything except lmmonai control. An Immortal can command a blackball, but it is beyond mortal control; fonunately, it _is_ extremely rare. It may be defeated by a gate spell. sending it to some other plane, or by a carefully worded _wish._ 

Despite their size and awkward walk, they move very quiecly and arrack without warning whenever they can. They surprise on a roll of 1-3 (on ld6) due to their stealth. When using weap- _ons,_ they add + I ro all arrack :md damage rolls because of their suength. 

When attacking, it "blinks" dose to an enemy. attacks, and then reappears ld4 x 10' away. If seriously threatened, an entire pack will "blink" out and not reappear. 

Though as intelligent as many humans, blink dogs do not speak human or demihuman lan· guages; they can communicate only among themselves. They like to live free the way wolves do and tend to come in conflict with huma.ns only when settlers encroach on their territories. They are carnivores, living on wild elk, moose, and other herd-beasts. 

In the wilderness, they live in smaii communities of 5·20 members, and send out hun ring packs of 2-16 fighteiS. They kill and eat herd animals whenever possible and sometimes raid farmers' grain storage sheds and meat-smoking sheds for food; in times of great hardship, they may kill humans for food. They are basicaiiy intelligent, using crude knives. dubs, and spears they make themselves; they know how ro use the superior weapons they sometimes steal from humans. There can be bugbear spellcasters; see " Monster Spellcasters." 

_Terr:lin:_ Any.

If a blast spore is damaged in any way. it ex· plodes for 6-36 (6d6) pointS of damage to all within 20'; each victim may make a saving throw vs. wands to take half damage. This explosion does not shower victims with spores the way the normal aru.ck does. 

_Monsrer Type:_ Boar: Normal Animal (Com· moo). Great Boar: Giant Animal (Rare). Wild boars generally prefer forested areas but can be found nearly everywhere. They are omnivores and have exuemely bad tempers when disturbed. They somecimes lie in thickets in the forest and charge passersby. They do have the charge anack special ability; if they can charge for 20 yards before reaching their prey, they inflier double damage when they hit. 

This giant gray wormiike creature _is_ about 30' long. They are meat-eaters and can be found nearly anywhere. 

Caeeilia often lie in wait in loose soil just below the surface. A viccim takes 1d8 points of damage each round until the victim or the caecilia is dead. _Terrain:_ Any except Arctic.

Great Boars: These ~e boars are huge and terrifying. They are most often found in " lost world" settings and are occasionally used as mounts by barbaric tribes.

ests, and open shrub lands. They arc extremely quick andl can outrun most prey over short distances. Panthers are usually black-furred. 

Camels are used as pack and riding animals in deserts and barren lands (with movement as if in clear terrain). A well-watered camel may travel for two weeks without drinking. Camels are herbivores, preferring grasses and grains, but will eat animal skin and bones when very hungry. 

The "great cats" arc large feline predators living in wilderness areas. They arc cautious, normally only attacking their natural prey, small herd-beasts. They will avoid fights with humans and demihumans unless forced by extreme hunger or when trapped with no escape route. 

Lion: Lions generally live in warm climates and thrive in savannah and brush lands ncar deserts. They usually hum in groups, known as prides. Male lions have the distinctive lionmane; female lions do not. 

A camel with one hump is called a dromedary, and one with two humps is a Bactrian camel. _Terr2in:_ Barren Lands (Bactrian), Desert (dromedary). _Lo2d:_ 3,000 en normal speed; 6,000 en half speed. 

Tiger: Tigers arc the largest of the commonly found great cats. They prefer cooler climates and wooded lands where their striped bodies offer some degree of camouflage. They often surprise their prey (1-4 on 1d6) when in woodlands. 

Great cats rarely go deeply into caves and usually remember a quick escape route to the out· doors. Despite their shyness, they arc very inquisitive and may follow a party out of curiosity. They will always chase a fleeing prey. 

_Barding Multiplier:_ X 1. 

Sabre-Tooth Tiger: Sabre-tooth tigers arc the largest and moSt ferocious of the great cats. They have oversized fangs, from which they get their name. Sabre-tooth tigers arc mostly extinct, except in "lost world" areas. 

Mountain Lion: This tawny-furred species lives mostly in mountainous regions but also inhabits forests and deserts. They will wander further into dungeons than any other species of great cat.

_Monster Type:_ Lowlife (Common). This scavenger is a 9'-long, 3'-high manylegged worm. It can move equally well on a floor, wall, or ceiling. Its small mouth is surrounded by eight tcmacles, each 2' long, which can paralyze on a successful hit unless a saving throw vs. paralysis is made. A tentacle hit does no actual damage. 

_Moasccr Type:_ Monster (Common). A centaur is a creature with the head, arms, and upper body of a man joined to the body and legs of a horse. They arc of average human intelligence and often carry weapons (dubs, lances, and bows; one weapon per crearurc). A centaur may use a charge attack with a lance. 

_Monster Type:_ Lowlife (Common). A giant centipede is a foot-long insect with many legs. Centipedes prefer dark, damp places and arc often found in dungeons or on the boles and branches of trees in deep forest. They do not commonly attack travelers, but will usually attack someone who disrurbs them. 

Carrion crawlers arc known as scavengers, eating the remains of sla.io animals. But they are also willing to go after fresh meat. They will attack small parties of travelers, paralyzing their prey, and will eat paralyzed victims in three turns un· less except when the carrion crawlers are being attacked. Unless magically cured , the paralysis will wear off in 2d4 turns. _Terrain:_ Cavern, Ruins. 

Centaurs will form into small tribes or families. Their homes arc in dense thickets or woods. The females and young will usuaUy stay in the lair. If attacked, females and young will attempt to flee; if escape is impossible, they will fight to the death. The young fight as 2-HD monsters, and do less damage (ld2/ld2/ld4). 

They attack by biting. The bite docs no damage to characters, but the victim must make a saving throw vs. poison or become violently ill for 10 days. Characters who do not make their saving throws move at half speed and will not be able to _perform_ any other physical action. The bite is more effective against very small creatures, such as the birds and insects they cat; such creatures must save vs. poison or die. _Terrain:_ Cavern, Ruins, Woods. 

There can be centaur spelkasters; see "Monster Spcllcasters." 

_Terrain :_ Woods, Open, Wooded Hills. _Lo2d:_ 3,000 en at full speed; 6,000 en at half speed.

mammals. All dinosaurs are very stupid (Intelligence 1-3) and easily fooled. 

_Monster Type:_ Monster (Rare). Though not strictly correct in the scientific sense, the game term "dinosaur" app lies to any prehistoric bird. fish, mammal, or reptile found in the Mesozoic or Paleozoic eras. Dinosaurs were the ancestors of modern birds, reptiles, and 

Each dinosaur can be placed in one of three categories: aquatic (mOstly marine) dinosaurs, landbased carnivores (meat eaters), and land-based herbivores (plant eaters). Use the general infor- 

mation given to create your own dinosaurs. You can create your own totally "new" dinosaurs, or base their descriptions on real dinosaurs. 

When assigning XP, treat them as having no special abilities unless they can swallow opponents whole (as noted in some descriptions). If you create your own dinosaurs, add an asterisk for each special ability (such as poison, throwing spikes. swoop, exceptional armor, and so on). 

Dinosaurs listed elsewhere in this book include: cave bear (bear). giant boar. giant crocodile, mastodon (elephant), pterosaur, sabretooth tiger (cats. great). triceratops, and ryrann052urus rex. 

Most aquatic dinosaurs are fish, turtles, or a combination of the two. Most are omnivorous, eating marine plants and a few small fish or other easy victims. The fins or flippers of any aquatic dinosaur may be used in defense, though this is not a normal attack form (use only if the dinosaur is in a frenzy). 

Small aquatic: Only primitive fish and eels fall into this category. Most flee if disturbed by anything 1 foot long or more. 

large aquatic: Some large land herbivores have marine counterparts. similar in appearance except for smaller legs, and fins instead of claws . Some look like snakes with unarmored turtlelike bodies. Only the largest aquatic dinosaurs have high morale. Carnivorous rypes will be more aggressive and territOrial. A very large specimen (20 + HD) may be able to swallow man-sized opponents on an anack roll of 20; treasure may be found inside its body. 

Armored aquatic: All the dinosaurs in this category are slow in comparison to other marine life, because of their large shells. They are the ancestors of modern turtles. 

_Terrain:_ River/Lake. Ocean (prehistoric)

## townsfolk. 

Wooddrake: These dark green drakes can change themselves into elf or halfling forms. They arc otherwise very similar in habits to mandrakes, and are sometimes discovered amidst elven or halfling communities. 

A drolem is a type of golem that looks like a dragon: it can be made to look like a dragon of any color. or may simply be a dragon skeleton. Like other golems, it is not alive, but a construct made by a high level magic-user or cleric. Drolems are extremely rare, made and used on- _ly_ to guard a special item or area. A special book and several rare materials arc needed to make a drolem. 

A drake is a man-sized creature that looks much like a dragon in iu normal form. However, it is most often encountered _polymorphed_ into a human or dcmihumao form. Drakes have no breath weapons or spcllcasting abilities. but they can talk. They may be: evil or good (50% chance of each) but, except for Elemental forms. arealways very Chaotic. Drakes are extremely intelligent and clever; they tell lies as needed, and surrender rather than fight to the death. 

Colddrake: These white drakes shun the light of day, living deep underground (usually in icy caverns). They can change themselves into dwarf or gnome forms, and can sometimes be found amidst an underground dwarf or gnome community. 

A drolcm is nonintelligent, and obeys its instructions exactly. It can see invisible things with· in 60', and is immune to _charm, hold, sleep,_ and all other mind-affecting spells, all forms of fire and cold, and all gases. It is also immune to all spells of 4th level or less, to normal and silver weapons, and even magical weapons of + 2 or lesser enchantment. 

Elemental Drake: There are four types: airdrakes (blue), carthdrakes (brown), firedrakes (red), and waterdrakes (sea-green). They have the same immunities as all drakes. Elemental drakes arc also immune to normal and silver weapons; a magical weapon is needed to damage them. They live on the elementa.l planes. and are very rare on the Prime Plane. They cannot oormalty travel bc:rwccn the planes. but may "ride" a.long with an elemental or other creature, either to or from their plane of origin. 

Drakes arc immune to all spells of 4th level or less. but may cancel this immunity for I round by concentrating- to _receive_ the benefitS of a _cure wounds_ spell. for example. 

In normal form, a drake looks similar to a small dragon without front legs and with tiny wings. These wings can only support slow flight, and only for an hour at a time. All drakes can _polymorph_ themselves into humanoid form (and back) as often as desired. In human or dcmihuman form, a drake can use any weapon permitted to thieves. An elemental is a magical, enchanted crearure that lives on another plane of existence (one of the elemental planes). It can be harmed only by magic or magical weapons. 

_ScaffEicmcmals_ (the weakest) are summoned by a magic-user with a special staff. _Device Elcmcncals_ arc summoned with the

use of a special miscellaneous magical item. _Conjured Elemencals_ arc summoned by the casting of the 5th level magic- user spell. To summon an elemental, a character must have a large amount of the element nearby (such as open air, bare earth, a pool of water or a bonfire). When the elcmemal arrives, it is hostile. and must be controlled by concentration at all times. The summoner's concentration is broken if he takes damage or fails any saving throw. The summoner can move only up ro half normal speed whjJe concentrating. 

However, an elemental cannot pass a _protection from evil_ spell effecL. 

An elemental will vanish if it or its summoner is slain, or when the summoner sends it back to its plane (which requires control), or if a _dispel magic_ is cast upon it. 

An _a.ir elemental_ appears as a great whirlwind, 2' tall and[1] /2" in diameter for each Hit Die (a staff elemental would be 16' tall and 4' across). ln combat, all victims of 2 HD or less hit by the whi rlwind must make a saving throw vs. death ray or be swept away. The elemcmal inflicts an extra IdS points of damage against any flying opponent. 

Lf the summon er's concentration is broken, the elemental will attack him. Once lost. control cannot be regained. The elemental can attack any creature between it and its summoner if it desires. 

An _earrh elemental_ appears as a huge manljke figure, 1' tall for each Hit Die (a spell-conjured elemental would be 16' tall). lt cannot cross a water barrier wider than its height. It inflicts an extra IdS points of damage against any opponent standing on the ground. 

If summoned in an area roo small for it (see size notes below), an elemental wi ll fill the available area-sideways. for example-possibly damaging the summoner in the process (and thus breaking the summoner's concentration).

Elementals live in towns and cities on their own worlds. Both the worlds and the building materials are made entirely of pure elememal material, in solid, liquid, or gaseous form. In the universe of its own plane, each elemental race occupies thousands of worlds. 

The elemental races arc far older than humankind, and more civilized in many ways. They have art forms for six senses. 

Some elcmcntals become clerics or magicusers in much the same ways as humans. However, an elemental mUst be an adult of _9_ or more Hit Dice before this knowledge can be learned. Many of the spells of the elememals are entirely different, and some cannot be cast by humans except when in elemental form. _Tcrrain:_ Elemental Planes.

_Monscer Type:_ Planar Monster, Enchanted (Very Rare). 

The statistics above apply only to elcmeotals encountered on their own planes of existence. On the Prime Plane, their abilities arc very limited. _One_ asterisk (for XP calculation) applies _only_ to eJcmcntals encountered on their own planes. 

Elemcntals are the dominant life forms on the elemental planes, and refer to themselves as "people." Size may range from I to 32 Hit Dice, and the rulers are much larger (50 Hit Dice at least, and possibly over 100). 

_Monscer Type:_ Planar Monster, Enchanted (Very Rare). 

These slow, huge creatures are identical to normal elcmentals, but far larger. They arc 2' tall per Hit Die. The number appearing applies per plane. Elemental rulers arc immune to 1st through 5th level spells, poison, all _charm, hold,_ and other mental attacks, illusions of all types, and any spell which could cause instant death (such as _disinregrace) ._ Weapons of + 3 or less _en-_ 

Their system of rule is similar to that of human Dominions. 

An elemental's normal form is a bloblikc shape. It can create "arms" as needed, to a maximum of 1 per Hit Die, but can only arrack with one blow per round. The elemental's material form is held togeth~r by its life force. The youn- 

chantmcnt have no effect on them. 

Any victim hit by an elemental ruler mUst make a saving throw vs. death ray or be crushed by the blow, instantly slain regardless of damage. Most of the victim's items and equipment are also destroyed by the blow (95% chance per item, -5% per "plus" if magical). However, any elemental struck by a ruler is not slain, but shattered into severa.l small elementals of 1 Hit Die each (the number of parts equal to half the original Hit Dice). 

All elemental rulers are friendly with and can su mmon most creatures of their respective planes. The creatures summoned will arrive as quickly as possible (usually from 3 rounds to 3 turns). 

The "Special" treasures of elemental rulers arc similar to those of human rulers, but unique to their respective planes. _Tcrrain:_ Elemental Planes.

Elephants a.re large, ponderous four-legged mammals. Though they are herbivores, they a.rc very dangerous creatures when frightened or when defending their young. These mighty crearurcs dwell at the edges of sub-tropical forests, living in medium to large herds. Both males and females have rusks. which arc valued at 100·600 gp per rusk for the ivory. 

ln combat, elephants attack with a charge, if possible, for double tusk damage. In the following rounds of combat they will either suike with their rusks (n%) or trample (25%). Elephants can be used as draft and riding animals. Some· rimes they arc equipped with barding and used as war-mounts. 

Prehistoric (Mastodon): This creature is a large, shaggy elephant. It has two mighty tusks that slope downward and then curve up and backward toward the elephant; they are a mighty battering weapon. Each rusk is worth 200-800 gp. Mastodons live in cold, icy lands or " lost worlds."

Stone Giants: These giants are 14' tall and have gray rod.l.ikc skin. They usc large stalactites as clubs. They often hurl rocks (ranges 100/200/ 300). They live in aves or crude stone huts, and may have 1d4 cave bears as guards (~0'111 chance). 

_Monster Type:_ Gia nt Humanoid (Hill Giants-Common, O thers- Rare) 

Giants arc huge humanlike monsters. The "lesser" forms _of_ giants (fire, frost, hill and stone) arc crudely-formed and ugly, while the "greater" races (cloud, mountain, sea and stoml) arc much more like humans in form and nature. 

Frost Giants: These awesome giants have pale skinandlightyclloworlightblue hair. Theystand 18' tall. have long full bards. and wear fur skins and iron armor. Frost giants may hurl rocks (rang· es 60/130/200). They often build castles above the timberline of snow-capped mountains. Frost giants always have either 3d6 polar bears {20% chance) or 6d6 wolves (80%) as guards. They arc not affected by cold-based attaclcs. 

Mountain Giants: These appear similar to stone or hill giants. 1bey arc hairy, have grayish skin, and stand 12' to 20' tall (usually 1' per Hit Die). 'Ibcy often (80%) carry boulders, and can throw them great distances (100/200/400), for 4d6 points of damage each. They arc usually reclusive but mercenary, and may be hlred to fight for any large force. ln melee combat, they usc huge swords or stone d ubs (for 1dl0 X~ damage). 

Giants either live solitary lives or live in com· munities of their own kind; in either case, they tend to live far away from human and demihuman civiHzations. There can be giant spell· casters (hill, stone, frost, fi re, cloud, and storm giants only); sec " Monster Spellcastcrs" in this chapter. 

Fire Giants: These giants have red skin and dark black hair and beards. They arc 16' tall and wear copper, brass, or bronze armor. They often throw rocks (ranges 60/130/200). Fire giants USU· ally make their home ncar volcanoes or other equally hot places. Their castles are often made of bladt baked mud reinfOKed with crude iron. They aiW1lys have cit.hct 1d3 hydras (20'111 chance) or 3d6 hellhounds (80'111) as guards. These giants arc not affected by fire-based attxb. 

Lesser giants arc usually willing to negotiate when cncounteted, as they have heard of the dangers of atuding _men._ Greater giants usually have no prejudice against adventurers and some· times will emenain them as guests. However, gi· ants stalcc out large tracts of land as their own and sometimes destroy human commun ities built in the lands they've claimed. Also, some few rogue giants develop habits which bring them into conflict with adventurers- such as a bandit's habit of robbery, a ghoul's taste for hu· man flesh, or an evil wiz.ard's desire to rule lesser beings. 

Sea Giants: These normally friendly creatures are rarely seen, preferring to live in the deepest canyons of the ocean depths. They appear ideotical to humans, except for their height ( 1 ~ · to 20' tall). Sea giants breathe water, but can hold their breaths for up to a full rum when venturing out of the sea (which is something they do very rarely). Though able to usc weapons (usually huge spears, doing 1d 10 X 4 damage), they rare· ly do so. They can push water with great force, creating a current (undetW1ltcr) in a cone-shaped area ~o· long and 30' wide at its base; aiJ within that area arc shoved 60' away from the giant at great speed (no saving throw), and each victim must make a saving throw vs. death ray or be stunned for ld6 rounds. On the surface, this cur· rent becomes a wave with the same effect but of grater size (120' long and 60' wide at the base), and inflicts 2d6 hull points of damage to any vessel i.n its path. 

Cloud Gi:uw: These fierce giants have white or gray skin and hair. They wear pale robes and Stand 20' tall. Ooud giants have keen eyes and a sharp sense of smell. so they arc rarely surprised (1 chance in 6). They may throw boulders (ranges 60/130/200). They live in castles in the sides of mountains or atop masses of douds. They keep ci· thcr ld6 small roes (in clouds or mount2.ins) or 6d6 dire wolves (only in mountains) as guards. Cloud giants hate to be disturbed and may block mountain passes to discourage trespassers. 

All giants can throw boulders as missile wcap· _ons,_ though the range varies. Any hit from a thrown boulder inflictS 3d6 points of damage. Throwing ranges in _yards_ (for outdoor cncount· crs) arc given for each giant. If encountered in a dungeon, the range should be read as feet.

Monsrer _Type:_ Construct, Enchanted (Rare). A golem is a "construct," a powerful, en· chanted monster created and animated by a high level magic-user or cleric. Golems can be made of almost any material. The DM should feel free to create new types as desired. 

Mud Go1em: A mud golem Stands about 6' tall and is shaped much like a muscular human fighter. It can swim or walk on the surface of mud and quicksand without sinking. It can re· main submerged in the subStances indefinitely without sinking, rising to the surface when it wishes. Mud golems hug their victims with both arms, trying to smother the victim in its body. Lf a mud golem hits, it will automatically cause 2d6 points of smothering damage each round there· after.

_Monster Type:_ Human (Rare) Headsmen (also called "executioners") are NPC humans commonl y employed by dominion rulers. They are trainc:tl in the business of killing criminals wbo have received the death penalty. Most headsmen are skilled in the proper use of bladed weapons, ropes, and poisons and are able to execute criminals quickly and neatly. 

## _Monster Type:_ Monster (Rare). 

This reddish-brown doglike monster is as big as a small pony. They are often found near volcanoes, deep in dungeons, or with other fire· loving creatures (such as fire giants). Hellhounds are cunning and highly intelligent. They can often _detect invisible_ (as the magic-user spell; 75% chance per round, range 60'). They are immune to normal fue, and make: all saving throws as fighters of equal Hit Dice. 

_Example:_ A 7 HD thug attempting to kill a 3 HD fighter has a chance of 50% plus 20% (for 4 HD difference in the thug's favor), or 70%. If the same thug tried to kill a 25th level fighter lord, the chance is 50% minus 10% (2 HD difference in the victim's favor), or 40%. Remem· ber that the fighter has only _9_ HD (despite his or her added hit points per level above chat), for a difference of only 2 Hit Dice in this example. 

All professional headsmen belong to their own guild, which is associated with the Thieves' Guild. Headsmen keep their uue identities completely secret, wearing hoods or disguises when engaged in professional activities. Many own ordinary shops, and can seem to be perfectly ordinary townsfolk. Headsmen of 6 HD or more are 90% undetectable in their disguises, and study Languages of all sons to improve their masquerades. Headsmen of 10 HD or more can even use the secret languages of other alignments.

_Monster Type:_ Planar Monster (Very Rare). "The hordes" arc life forms native to the elememal plane of Earth. Each single life force has hundreds of separate inscctlike bodies. The size of the bodies ranges from 3 to 21 feet long; the length corresponds to the Hit Dice (i.e., a 3-HD body will be 3' long). Details on the individual _bodies_ are given above. 

One horde life force can control up to 10.000 Hit Dice of bodies. Replacement bodies can be created at the rate of I Hit Die per turn. Unlike insects, there is no "queen" body: the life force is widely spread, occupying all the bodies evenly. The life force can only control bodies within a volume 100 miJes across: if taken outside that range, a body becomes a mindless thing, dying 

in 1-10 days. Each planet in the realm of the hordes is occupied by 1d100 life forces . 

Each individual life force has its own name. All the bodies of a single life force will respond to the same name, and this can cause confusion in dealing with a horde creature. The creature it· self can only die if _all_ of its bodies arc desuoyed. 

The horde crearures do not consider any other life forms to be imdligem. When a horde needs more room, it will simply try to take it, without regard for other creatures: thus, they arc considered evil. The horde creatures often grapple with each other in this war for living space. 

A horde creature can usc _ESP_ and _telekinesis_ (up to 2,000 en) _as_ often _as_ desired, up to once per round. It communicates by _rclepachy,_ speaking directly to the minds of others. It is incredibly intelligent, and can easily handle dozens of conversations at once. 

Each horde is very Lawful and always dangerous. A horde creature sacrifices _as_ many _bodies_ as needed to reach a goal, and thus the morale of a body is 12. The creature is immune to all mental effects (charm, _bold, sleep,_ etc.), but the bodies are susceptible to blows and damage-cawing at· tacks of most rypes. Because of its disregard for individual bodies, a horde normalJy docs not bother to attempt to save them; in play, it simply fails all saving throws voluntarily. However, if 10% or more of a horde's _bodies_ arc lost in a single acciviry (an encounter with enemies. for example), the creature will either resolve the problem peacefully (negotiating, avoiding, etc.) or calJ other hordes for assistance. 

Each horde can have a different species of insect _as_ its bodies. One horde might consist of bodies which look l.ikc huge gold praying manrises with wings, whiJc another might consist of smallish black beetles with glowing red tips on their antennae. 

The hordes' enemies arc the kryst and the undines. They fear fife-type creatures and attacks. _Terrain:_ Plane of Earth.

_Monster Type:_ Normal Animal (Common). Horses are four-legged equines already familiar to players. They' re herbivores: they run wild in the plains and can be tamed _as_ riding-beasts. Riding Horse: This beast can carry a rider for a greater distance than any other rype of horse. It is smaller, and can exist wherever there is grass to 

feed on. MOSt wild horses on the plains fall into the "riding horse" category once tamed. War Horse: This type of horse is bred for its warlike temperament and _suength._ Unlike other horses, it is trained to charge. When charging, its rider can do double damage when using a lance. The horse cannot fight while charging, 

and cannot move at charging speed for more than three rounds at a _time._ 

Draft Horse: This is a large horse bred for sturdiness and endurance. It is used mostly _as_ a pack animal, or for plowing or pulling wagons. A draft horse will not fight; if attacked, it will flee. 

Pony: This is a small horse, preferred as a riding mount by many human children, halflings and dwarves. _Terrain :_ Open. 

_Load:_ Riding Horse: 3,000 en of weight at normal rates, or 6,000 en at half normal. War Horse: 4,000 en at normal rates, or 8,000 en at half normal. Draft Horse: Pulls 4.~00 en at normal rates, or 9,000 en at half normal. Pony: 2,000 en at normal rates. or 4,000 en at half normal. _Barding Multiplier:_ X l.

A clerical lich normally has 3d4 types of other undead nearby, acting as servants. A full lair of each type (maximum number appearing) is usually present. 

Either type of lich can summon other powerful undead for aid. The summons can be made simply by concenuating. and the creature(s) responding arrive 1d100 rounds later, depending on their distance. The summons may be made as often as desired, but any one type of creature will respond only once per day at _most._ To randomly determine the creatures appearing in an· swer to the summons, roll 1d20 and refer to the table. Roll again if a type of creature has already responded that day. 

_Monster Type:_ Undead, Enchanted (Very Rare). 

A lich is a powerful undead monster of magical origin. It looks like a skeleton wearing fine garments, and was _once_ an evil and chaotic magic-user or cleric of level 21 or greater (often 27-36). A lich is sciJJ able to use spciJs as it did while alive, so it is exuemely dangerous. A lich is not normally found wandering, but instead remains in or very near a well-defended lair. Such a lair might be a dungeon, catacomb, tomb, or necropolis ("city of the dead").

The very sight of a lich causes fear in all char· acters below ~th level (no saving throw). Its merest touch causes 1d 10 points of damage, and can paralyze any creature for 1d100 days (though a saving throw applies. and the paralysis is magically dispellable). 

Before any encounter with a lich, the OM should select spells for the creature. This should be done with care, as a lich is extremely intelligent and uses them to its best advantage. Note that the lich's morale is given as 10, but a lich flees if in actual danger. 

A summoned vampire may (n% chance; check for each) be a magic-user or cleric of level 7·9 (1d3 + 6). 

Liches are undead, and can be turned (but not desuoyed) by clerics. They are immune to _charm, sleep, fecblemind, polymorph, cold, lighrning,_ and _death_ spells, and can be harmed _only_ by magical weapons. They are _also_ immune to the effects of all spells of less than 4th level. 

Liches are master villains, coordinating armies and spy-networks made up of the undead. Each one has its own goal: One may wam to achieve true Immortality, one may serve an evil Immortal ofEmropy, one may wish to uansform the entire world imo a horrid playground for the undead. Each licb in a campaign should have its own name, style, and motivation. _Terrain:_ Ruins.

_Monster Type:_ Monster, Enchanted (Common). l ycanthropcs arc humans who can change imo beasts (or in the case of wercrats, beasts who can change into humans). They normally wear no armor, since it wouJd interfere with their shapechanging. Any lycanthrope: can summon ld2 normal animals of its type:: wcrcbcars can summon normal bears, werewolves can summon normal wolves, and so forth. Summoned animals will arrive in 1d4 rounds. 

Some animals (such as horses) do not like the smell oflycanthropcs and wiJI react with fear. If a lycanthrope: _is_ hit by wolfsbane, it must make a saving throw vs. poison or run away in fear. The sprig of wolfsbane must be swung or thrown as a weapon, using normal combat procedures. A lycanthrope: returns to its "noanal" form when kiJJcd . 

_Animal_ Form: In animal form, a lycanthrope: can be harmed only _by_ magical weapons, silvered weapons, or spc:IJs. The lycanthrope: cannot speak normal languages, tho ugh it can speak with normal animals of its wcrctype. 

Human _Form :_ ln human form, a lycanthrope often looks somewhat like its wcrcform. Wererats have longer noses, wcrcbears arc hairy, werebats have long arms, wcrefoxcs arc sly and nimble, and so forth. In this form, they can be attacked with normaJ weapons, and they may speak any known languages. 

Lycanthropy: l ycanthropy is a disease. Any human character who loses more than half of his hit points in battJc with a lycanthrope becomes a lycanthrope: of the same type: in 2d 12 days. The disease kills dcmihumartS. The victim begins to show signs of the disease in half that time. The cond ition can be cured only by a cleric of lith level or gre:uer, who will do so for a suitable price 

or service. Any character who becomes a full lycanthrope will become an NPC, to be ruo by the OM only. 

## _Common Lycanthropes_ 

Wcrcrat: Wcrcrats arc different from most ly - canthropes because the were-animal form is their natural form, and human form is the shape th ey assume. They arc intelligent, can speak Common in either form, and can usc any weapon. A wererat usually prefers to use a man-sized rat form, but can become a full-sized human. Wererats arc sneaky and often set ambushes, surprising on a roll of 1-4 (on ld6). They summon giant rats to help them in battle. Only a wererar's bite causes lycanthropy. 

Werewolf: These creatures are semi-intelligent and usually hunt in packs . Any group of 5 or more will have a leader with 30 hit points, who anacks as a ) Hit Dice monster, add ing + 2 to damage rolls. Werewolves summon no rmal wolves to form large packs with them . 

Wereboar: Were boars arc semi-intelligent and bad-tempered. In human form they often seem _co_ be berserkets, and may act the same way in bat de (gaining + 2 on attack rolls and fighting to the death). Wercboars summon normal boars to help them in battle. Wcrcboars do not associate with devil swine. 

Weretiger: These relatives of the great cats often act like them , being very curious but becoming dangerous when threatened. They are good swimmers and qu iet trackers, surprising often (1-4 on ld6). They can summon any type of great cat that is in the area (preferring tigers). Werebear: Were bears arc very intelligent, even in animal form . A werebear usually prefers to live alone or with bears. It might be friendly, however, if peacefully approached. In combat. wcrebears can hug for 2d8 points of damage (in addition to normal damage) if both paws hit the same target in one round . A werebear can summon any type of bear in the area. 

## _lJnconnnJonLycanthropes_ 

Werebat: Th ese dangerous flying creatu res arc sometimes confused with vampires, rurning from human to bat form at will. In addition to summoning normal and giant batS, they can summon Id4 other werebars (each of which can, in turn, summon other normal or giant bats, but not more wcrebats). Each wcrcbat bite may inflict a nonmagical disease (of the OM's choice); th e chance is I in 6, checked per bite. 

Werefox: Where dense underbrush slows most normal movement to half or less, this creature can maintain fu ll or rwo-thirds normal movement. It also normally has high imelligcncc, and thus often becomes a magic-user as well (though spells can be cast only when in human form). A wcrefox can also _charm_ (petsons in pe:rson form, animals in fox form) three times per day; however, this effect lasts for 24 hours at most. 

Wercshark: These are mermen, inflicted with a form of lycanthropy that enables them to rake the form of a mako shark anytime they choose so long as it is in darkness. When the m oon is full

> The manscorpion is an evil combination of man and arachnid . The upper body is like that of a human , but irs lower parts arc those of a giant scorpion (with stinging tail). lr may be found in nearly any climate, but most frequently in deserts, moumains, and dungeons. 

This arachnid warrior normally wields a huge pole arm (damage 3d6 points), but may usc a long bow or a ny other weapon available. It may also strike with its dreaded deadly poisonous tail; the victim hit takes Id 10 points of damage , a nd must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Even if the saving throw is successful , the victim is paralyzed for 0-7 rounds (IdS-!). Only victims immune to paralysis or poison can avoid this effect, so the monsters are greatly feared. They arc immune to their own poison and to the poison of all scorpions. 

_Monscer Type:_ Planar Monster, Enchanted (Very Rare). 

A malfe ra is a creature from the Dimension of Nightmares, where many evil dreams arc bred and released imo the minds of sleeping people. A maJfera appears only through the acts of a powerful magic-user or an Immortal; its dimension is believed poisonous and deadly to humans. 

Some ( I in 20) of the arachnid creatures are clerics, of 8th-13th level (with the corresponding added Hit Dice). However, these are normally found only in their lair. 

The: malfera has a large, elcphantlikc face and a shon trunk. The head is topped by large horns. Large fangs protrude from either side of the trunk. The chest is a mass of slimy. short tentacles. Long. muscular arms end in large , jagged pincers. Its feet arc webbed and clawed. It is colored night-black but has red veins and eyes. 

Manscorpions arc intelligent warlike beings whose main interests involve acquiring food and destroying creatures different from them . They do not make friends with other sentient races and make pets only of giant scorpions. They make raids on desert human communities for food and attack any liv ing thing that ventures into their territories.

A manticore _is_ a horrid monster with the body of a lion, leathery bat wings, a ta.il ridged with spikes, and the face of a mao with large. sharp fangs. It usually lives in wild mouma.in ranges. The manticore has 24 ta.il spikes, and can shoot six each round even when flying (ranges 50/100/180). The creature regrows rwo spikes per day. Its favorite food is man. 

Mamicores frequently track humans, ambushing them with spike attacks when the human group stops to rest. Another tactic _is_ to stalk its prey like a great cat, creeping up close on an unsuspecring vicrim. When that victim _is_ alone. the manticore fires off a barrage of tail-spikes to bring the victim down. The manticore then cats the victim. Less frequently, a pack of manticores will stalk and attack a group of vicrims. _Tcrrain:_ Mountain.

Dervish: Dervishes are desen raiders. About 90% are fighters; the rest are clerics. Dervishes often form camps or tribes of up to 300 men, led by a lOth level cleric. Such a camp will be either tents (75%) or a wooden or brick stockade (25% ). These camps contain their women, children, livestock, and their treasure. 

Brigand: Brigands are _loosely_ organized oudaws and renegade mercenaries who live by raiding towns and robbing caravans and travelers. Most belong ro the fighter class. For every 20 brigands there is one additional 2nd level fighter who acts as their leader. For every 40 brigands there is an additional 4th level fighter acting as commander of the entire group. 

> Dervishes are noted for their fanatic belief in their philosophies and their intolerance of other views. On rare occasions, they will wage a holy war in which they attempt ro capture or kill all who have different beliefs. Captives are given an opportunity to convert; if they refuse, they may be killed or enslaved. Lawful characters may be invited ro join the crusade, and those who refuse will be viewed with great suspicion unless a good reason can be provided as ro why they should not participate.

_Monsrer Type::_ Normal Animal (Common). Snakes arc long, sinuous, legless reptiles. They come in rwo varieties: constrictors and vipers. Consuictors wrap around their prey and squeeze it to death (they can bite, too, for some damage); vipers bite their prey and inject poison. Snakes are found almost everywhere, avoiding only very cold places. Most snakes do not usually attack unless surprised or threatened. Most snakes are carnivores but prefer prey small enough for them to eat; when dining. they unhinge their jaws and swa.llow their prey whole.

The combination of pits and infravision makes it very hard to fight a pit viper; it is _so_ quick that it always gains the initiative (no roll needed). Any victim bitten by a pit viper must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. 

Spitting Cobra: A spirting cobra is a 3' long grayish-white snake. It spitS a stream of venom at its victim's eyes, up to a distance of 6' away. As with most small poisonous snakc.s, a spitting cobra will not attack human-sized or larger opponentS unless stanled or threatened. It can either spit or bite in one round, but not

_Monsccr Type:_ Planar Monster, Enchanted (Very Rare). 

Spectral hounds are creatures from the Dimensional Vorrex- rhe void between all dimensions. In this world they appear as ghostly dogs-pale in color and translucent. Their eyes are formless pools of utter blackness. They arc excellent trackers and once on the trail of a creature, they follow it for days. They arc bred and trained by interplanar beings (such as elemental rulers, amirs, pashas, etc.) as hunting animals, and are sometimes used to track intrusive adventurers back to their home planes. Likewise, adventurers mighr be able to _charm_ spectral hounds and train them to track villains through the planes. Spectral hounds never come to the Prime Plane except when being used in this manner by greater powers. 

In combat, a spectral hound anacks by biting. Any character binen by a spectral hound must save vs. spells. If he saves, the character suffers only the 2d6 points of damage from the bite. if he fails to save, he begins to fade. This fading is very gradual: In 24 hours the charaner has faded to the same translucent appearance as a spectral hound. The character's equipment is not affected. When rhe charaner finishes fading completely, he is unable ro hold any normal items. He is unable to hear or talk 10 unfaded characters. From the faded character's point of view. all normal things appear translucent, while faded things (i .e. the spectral hounds and other affected characters) seem solid and normal.

_Monsccr Type:_ Monster (Rare). A sphinx is a large. winged creature with alion's body and a human's face . It is fond of dry climates, bur may be encountered anywhere, most often as a guard. Some Chaotic sphinxes are very territorial, settling on a hilltop near a road and preventing all travelers from passing along that road . 

Both male and female sphinxes arc very imelligcm spellcasters, the female a 12th level cleric and the male a 12 level magic-user. Their magic is so powerful that all saving throws against their spells arc made with a -4 penalty. 

_Monster Type:_ Undead, Enchanted (Rare). The ghostly spectres arc among the mightiest of the undead. They have no solid bodies; they appear as translucent beings of evil expression. their eyes fiery and red or black and featureless. Once human _or_ demihuman, they have risen af. ter death tO do evil. They are often used as lieutenants by greater evil powers. 

In combat, a sphinx can attack with claws and bite (or spells), but its most feared attack is its roar. The roar is usable only twice per day, but is quite powerful. Each victim within 120' must make a saving throw vs. spells at a _-4_ penalty or flee in _fear_ for ld6 turns. Each victim within 60' must check for _fear_ (as above) and must also make a saving throw vs. paralysis or be stunned for 1-6 rounds. (Sec the "Special Character Conditions" section of Chapter 13 for more _on_ the effects of srunning.) Each victim within 10' must check for _fear_ and _srun_ (as above), but also takes 6d6 points of damage, and is deafened for ldlO turns (no saving throw). 

They can only be hit by magical weapons; silver weapons have no effect. like all undead, spectres arc immune to _sleep, charm._ and _hold_ spells. 

A hit by a spectre 1nflins IdS points of damage in addition to a double energy drain (the victim loses two experience levels). A character slain by a spectre will rise the next night as a spectre under the control of the slayer. _Terrain:_ Ru ins. 

The sphinx is immune _to_ all 1st, 2nd, and 3rd level spells and to nonmagical weapons. It loves puzzles, riddles, and trivia. Characters may avoid combat or gain the sphinx's friendship by solving the sphinx's riddles. 

If two sphinxes arc encountered together. they arc a mated pair; if more than two arc encountered, they are a mated pair with cubs. _Terrain:_ Any; especially Desert.

Tarantella: A tarantella is a huge hairy magical spider that looks like a 7' long tarantula. Its bite does nor kill; instead, it causes the victim (if a saving throw vs. poison is failed) to have painful spasms that resemble a frantic dance. This dance has a magical effect on onlookers. Anyone watching the dance muse make a saving throw vs. spells or stan to dance in the same way. Dancing victims have a penalty of -4 on their attack rolls, and attackers gain + 4 on their attack rolls. The effects of the bite last for 2d6 turns. However, dancers will drop from exhaustion in 5 turns, and they will then be helpless against attacks. Those caught while watching will dance as long as the original victim. (A _dispel_ magic spell will stop the dance.) _Terrain:_ Crab: Cavern, Ruins. Black Widow, Tarantella: Ruins, Woods. 

_Monster Type:_ Planar Monster (Vcty Rare). The "planar spiders" are intelligent planetraveling arachnids with a vast, but odd, civilization. They can travel through planes and dimensions at will. Those most commonly encountered have 5 Hit Dice, but leaders of up to 12 Hit Dice have been found . Their home plane is not known, and no traces of cities have ever been discovered; planar spiders describe it as a world covered with cities made up of buildings lovingly crafted from imperishable white webs. Planar spiders are widely-enough traveled that most speak Common. 

Crab Spider: This is a 5' long spider with a chameleon like ability to blend into its surroundings, surprising on a roll of 1-4 (on ld6). It clings to walls or ceilings and drops onto its prey. After the first anack, it can be seen and anacked normally. Any victim of its bite must make a saving throw vs. poison or die in ld4 turns. However, the poison is weak, and the victim gains a + 2 bonus to the saving throw roll. 

Black Widow Spider: This vicious arachnid is 6' long, and has a red "hourglass" mark on its belly. It usually stays close to its webbed lair. The webs should be ueated as the magic-u.ser's _web_ spell for the of breaking free, once en- 

In combat, a planar spider arrives from another plane (usually the Ethereal), attacks, and then "shifts" back to the other plane. It automatically gains initiative when "shifting," and usually (75%) cannot be attacked before it leaves! However, _hasted_ opponents may attack normally before the creature "shifts." 

Normally, any victim bitten must make a saving throw vs. poison with a -4 penalty to the roll, or die. However, the creature can choose to bite without using the poison, if desired. 

Any spider encountered may have ld3 miscellaneous magical items that it can use. or it may have ld4 odd but nonmagical items with which it- but not humans-is familiar. 

Occasional rare encounters may be with spellcasting planar spider clerics or magic-users (maximum 9th level in either). For XP calculations, one asterisk is added for each rwo levels of spell use. Plana.r spiders that cast spells cannot cast spells and then phase out in the same round. Planar spiders will not autOmatically anack PCs. In fact, since they' re the primary intelligence of their own planes, they should be played much like humans. There could be planar-spider bandits, NPC adventuring parties, etc. Most, when encountered, will speak to PCs and find out their intentions toward him: This could be a real surprise to charancrs who have only encountered "normal" giant spiders! _Terrain:_ Any.

Druj: Druj appear as body parts, floating or crawling about in a horrible way. A druj is usually encountered in the form of a hand, eye, or skull. Druj are very intelligent and strongly evil, far more dangerous than they may seem. 

Once it has seuled for the night, an odic cannot move from the spot until daybreak. Whi le using its spells, it can attack by animating pan of the plant. The longest branch or vine of the plant reaclhes out ( 10-30' range), attacking as a 16 HD monster and inflicting ldl2 points of damage per hit (in addition to poison). 

A druj can split its essence, creating four (identical) forms instead of one. This can be performed only once per night. Each of the forms can anack separately, but on ly one of the forms is able to cast spells (as given above). The form us· ing the spells can often be distinguished, as it will hover nearby while the other forms auack. If that form is slain, one of the surviving forms im· mediately gains all unused spcllcasting abilities. All four forms are poisonous. 

Druj only: First successful turn anempt forces druj components to reunite; subseq uent turn rolls handled normally. 

The plant is immediately killed when the odic possesses it. The crt-ature uses the plant's parts to seek out other life to feed on. Most commonly, it animates individual leaves, which float away (movement rate 30' per round) in search of victims; it can animate up to 6 such leaves at one lime. The leaves may be scm up to I mile &om the odic. Ani· mated leaves normally gain surprise (90% chance). Each leaf attacks as if a 4 Hit Dice monster; no damage is inflicted, but each victim hit must make a saving throw vs. spells or be _charmed._ A _ch:umcd_ victim is drawn toward the odic, and has a -4 penairy on the saving throw against the energy drain when entering the purple aura. 

_Monscer Type:_ Undead. Enchanted (Very Rare). 

Spirits are powerful evil beings inhabiting the bodies (or body parts) of others; they arc among the nastiest of undead monsters. They are immunc to spells below 4th level, and cannot be harmed by normal weapons or magical weapons of less than + 2 enchantment. 

lf rurned by a cleric, the pans of a druj turned arc forced lO reunite into one creature, remaining united for ld4 + I rounds. Further success at turning is handled normally. 

All spirits arc travelers. never staying in one place for more than one night: they become invisible and nearly powerless (except to move) with the light of dawn, rega.ining their powers at dusk. In daylight, any spirit can travel up to 24 miles per day (I hex). 

Druj are always encountered singly unless commanded into service by a lich or more powerful member of the Sphere of Death. In such cases, two druj eyes may rest within a druj skull, accompanied by two druj hands; no more than these five druj can ever gather in one place. 

If the plant possessed has no detachable leaves. the odic may animate other portions (pine needles, flowers, etc.) in a similar manner, as described above-up to 6 at once, each with a _charm_ ability per touch. 

> All spirits arc poisonous. When hit by a spirit in hand·to-hand combat, the victim must make a saving throw vs. poison or die immediately. A new saving throw must be made for each hit by the spirit. 

_Eye:_ An eye druj darts about, trying to touch (poison) its opponent; a touch docs not inflict any damage other than poisoning. Each eye druj can also gaze at one victim per round (30' range), in addition to its physical attack. The victim must make a saving throw vs. paralysis or be paralyzed for ld4 turns. The eye druj may touch a paralyzed victim automatically. 

Odics occasionally inhabit the bodies of p lantlike monsters. The creature may make a saving throw vs. spells to avoid the possession, but may die from the level draining and other abilities of the odic even if the saving throw is successful. The odic gains the abilities of any plantlike monster possessed. They may be used in addition to the normal abilities of rhe odic. Odics arc always encountered singly. 

The poisonous presence of a spirit causes all consumable items within 30', including normal food and water, holy water, all rations (even iron) and even magical potions to become spoiled and useless (but not poisoned). with no saving throw allowed. Even living plants and small insects with· in this area arc paralyzed. dying if the spirit remains there more than an hour. This effect negates all forms of plant control, insect swarms and plagues, both normal and magical. 

_Hand:_ A hand druj inflicts !d4 points of damage when it hits, and thereafter holds onto its victim, causing automatic damage each round thereafter. The damage caused is equal to the AC of the victim, ignoring dexterity and shield bonuses. plus ld4 pointS. If the adjusted armor class is a negative number. the auack will still inflict ld4 points of damage each round. 

Revenant: This horror appears to be a zombie, though it walks at a faster rate. It never carries weapons. The revenant roams the night in search of victims. surprising them 50% of the time. It can leap once per tum to a 60' range; when both surprising and leaping on a victim. its three at· tacks all hit (no attack rolls needed). causing normal damage and three separate saving throws vs. poison. 

All spirits can sense invisible things. and can at· tack them without penalty. All spirits can, once per round, at will, create the following cleric spell cfftctS: _darknos. silence 15' radius,_ cause _disease,_ animace _dead. finger_ of _death_ (all as if cast by a 16th level cleric). A spirit will often pause to _ani-_ marc the body of a fallen victim. creating and controlling it as a zombie to fight for it and add to the chaos. (Attempts at turning such zombies are made as if turning the spirit itself!) All of these spell-like abilities require concentration. as do normal spells, so while using an ability, a spirit cannot attack physically. Unlike normal cleric spells, no words or gestures are needed. 

_Skull:_ A skull druj floats tOw:ud and bites its victim. When first approached, the victim must make a saving throw vs. spells or be frozen with fear, allowing the skull druj to bite (no attack roll needed) for 2d4 points of damage. The normal saving throw vs. poison applies to each bite. 

Once per night, a revenant can _summon_ !d4 spectres to come to its aid. The spectres will arrive ld6 + 2 rounds after being summoned, and will obey and fight for the revenant. They may be turned as normal spectres. 

Odic: This evil spirit travels up to 24 miles each day. settling into a plant by night. It is dangerous even if avoided, as it animates parts of the plant to do its bidding. The plant can easily be seen at long range (up to 300 yards), as the odic radiates a purplish light in a 20' radius. Any living being within this light must make a saving throw vs. spells or lose I level because of energy drain (as if struck by a wight). 

RevenantS arc resistant to turning attemptS. lf any "D" result is indicated, the revenant may make a saving throw vs. spells; if successful, the: at· tempt has no effect. A "tum" result gives no saving throw, but the revenant will return in !d4 turns. Rcvenams are always encountered singly. _1i:rrain:_ Any (usually Barren Lands and Ruins). 

A spirit normally has no treasure, though it may occasionally serve as a guard for some special item. Those characters who risk travel at night may encounter a spirit with ld6 of irs victims, who may carry treasure.

_Monscer Type:_ Monster (Very Rare). The sporaclc appears identical to a beholder at first glance: a floating ball-like creature.~· in diameter, with a huge gaping mouth :tnd a large central eye above it. Tentacles sprout from itS entire body. It has six eyes. positioned evenly about the surface of the body (top, bottom. front; back, sides). It normally keeps all but a few upper tcnracles retracted . 

A sporaclc regenerates by submersing itSelf in fresh water (but not in brine) at the rate of 3 hit points per round so lost body pans may be rapidly regrown. If a loose tentacle falls or is placed in water, it will grow into a whole creature in I hour. This is their only method of reproduction, _so_ they are often found ncar a water source. 

A sporacle may attack anything. but prefers humanoids as food. As it moves into combat, it extends all itS tentacles, appearing to sprou t them as it attacks. It moves through air or water _by_ magical flight, but is _very_ quick. It spins rapidly in all directions when 10 combat , wing all of its tentacles each round agatnst I or 2 opponents. A sporaclc has average intelligence {10) and cannot usc spells or magical items. 

The sporacle prefers not 10 bite victims that are still moving. It uses itS tentacle attacks only. until all have been destroyed ; only then will it resort to its ferocious bite. Each tentacle hit inflicts I point of damage. and each requires a saving throw vs. paralysis. Failure indicates that the venomous tentacle has struck skin, and takes effect. This paralysis is a delayed sort, however. taking effect after 1 round passes; it lasts for 1 turn thereafter unless cured. If its opponents flee. it will remain to feast upon its paralyzed victims; if there are none, it :tlways pursues. 

The sporacle may be damaged by any sort of edged weapon, and by any missile wca.pon except a sling. However. it is immune to blunt weapons. and to all spells and magical devices except those that cause damage; these will destroy one tentacle per die of damage (or per _magic missile)._ not affecting the creature's hit points. Once all the tentaelcs arc destroyed. such spells have no further effect. Sporades cannot hear, and arc immune to all sound-based effects; they are also immune to poison, paralysis. and charms. 

If any attacker declares the tentacles to be the target of the blow. and wcs an edged weapon. the tentacle is AC 4, and easily severed. After falling off, a tentacle will live for up co I hour. remaining venomous for that time. When the creature is reduced to 0 hit points or less. its body comes apart grotesquely. spinning wildly and sending all remaining tentacles in various directions. (Make final attack rolls as app licable.) _Terrain:_ Cavern.

lron: A living iron statue has a _body_ that can absorb iron and steel. It takes normal damage when hit. but if a nonmagical metal weapon is used, the attacker must make a saving throw vs. spells or the weapon will become stuck in the body of the living iron st.atue, and can only be removed if the statue is killed. (If the weapon is left in the statue, the statue will eventually ab· sorb the metal completely and eject nonmetal pans. so the statue will not forever walk around with weapons sticking out of it.) 

_Monsrer Type:_ Construct, Enchanted (Commoo). 

A living starue is an enchanted animated crcarure made by a powerful wizard. It appears to be a perfectly normal statue- until it moves! A living statue may be any size or material ; the sizes given are typical. Living crystal, iron, and rock statues are given as examples. and the OM may create others. (Not every statue in a campaign should be a living statue. If every statue in _your_ campaign is a living statue, PCs will know that any statue they see can attack them , Have noblemen possess statuary as treasure and decoration; have expensive public buildings and plazas be decorated with statues; living statues are very rare in comparison with the numbers of "real" statues.) 

Rock: A living rock statue has an outer crust of stone but is filled with hot magma (fiery lava). When the creature attacks, it squirtS the magma from its fingertips (or similar members) for 2d6 points of damage per hit. 

_Terrain :_ Any (especially Ruins). 

_Load:_ Crystal Statue: 1 ,~00 en at full speed; 3,000 en at half speed. _leon_ Statue: 2,000 en at full speed ; 4.000 en at half speed. Rock Starue: 2,500 en at full speed; 5.000 en at half speed. 

Living statues are not affected by _sleep_ spells. Crystal: A living crystal statue is a life form made of crystals instead of flesh. Crystal statues can look like statues of anything. but often appear human.

_Monster Type:_ Prehistoric Animal (Very Rare). 

_Monster Type:_ Monster (Rare). A treant is an 18' tall, intelligent creature that looks like a tree with facial features. It has two main branches that act as arms with hands. and it walks upon legs that end in rootlike feet. 

_Monscer Type:_ Giant Animal (Common). Giant Toad: A giant toad is about the size of a very large dog. and weighs 150-250 pounds. It can change its skin color to blend into woods or poorly lit dungeons, surprising its prey on a roll of 1-3 (on ld6). It can shoot its tongue out to 15', and may drag victims of dwarf size or smaller to its mouth to be bitten. Small prey is swallowed whole on a attack roll of 20, causing id6 points of dam:~ge each round thereafter. 

This is an armored herbivorous dinosaur. It walks about on four legs and has much the same temperament as an elephant. The triceratops is about 30' long and weighs I 0-12 tons. A collarlike armor plate grows from its head to protect its neck, and its weapons include a short horn growing from its snout and two long horns growing above its eyes. A single triceratops is a match for all but the largest of the predatory carnosaurs. 

It is concerned only with the protection of forests and plant life; it is friends with most of the intelligent forest creatures (actaeons. centaurs, dryads, etc.). Treants speak a slow and difficult tongue, and distrust those who use fire. 

All encounters with creams begin at a distance of 30 yards or less, since they a.re ne:1rly identical to normal trees, and they surprise on a roll of 1-3 (on ld6). Although normal weapons can harm them, blum weapons (such as maces) only inflict I point of damage per hit (plus magic and strength bonuses). 

Rock ToadfCave Toad: A rock toad, or "cave toad". lives in rocky. cold regions such as high mountains or frozen desens. h is about the size of a large dog. weighs 150 pounds. and carries a hard, bumpy shell on its back (like a tunic). On its head. it h:IS bulging. multi-faceted eyes similar to a fly's. The eyes shine with a hypnotic glow. Any creature gazing into the eyes must save vs. paralysis. or be paralyzed for 2-8 (2d4) rounds. The eyes will continue to cast a feeble light (5' radius) for ld3 hours after the creature dies, but the hypnotic powers will be lost. When attacking. it bites with a horny. beaked mouth. _Terrain:_ Giant Toad: Cavern; Woods (ncar water). Rock/Cave Toad: Cavern ; Descn (cold), Mountain. 

Although it is an herbivore, it is aggressive and dangerous, usually anacking on sight. It might _charge_ (for double damage) on the first attack, and on any attack after it has gotten 20 yards or more away from its enemy. 

_Terrain :_ Open (prehistoric). _Load:_ 10,000 en at full speed; 20,000 en at half speed. 

Each ucant can animate any two trees within 60' to move at 30' (10') and fight :IS treants. A ueam may change which trees it is animating from round to round.

## **Basic Ways to Vary Monsters** 

To determine the Intelligence of an individual, find the average Intelligence of its race from the monster description. Go to the line corresponding to that score on the Monster Intelligence table. Roll rwo six-sided dice (2d6). The first die is used to determine how much this individual's Intelligence va.ries from the race's average; move across 10 the column corresponding to the number you rolled. The second die is used to determine whether to subtract (H) or add (4-6) this amount from the race's average. 1Ieat results of less than 0 as 0 and results of greater than 18 _as_ 18. Vampires and lowlifes ignore subtractions.

## **Age** 

Consider the average number of hit points per Hit Die as a renection of a monster's age. A newborn creature would have I hit poim per Hir Die (the minimum) and gradually gains more hit points as it :~ges. The average score (4[1] /z points per die on the average) is reached at the prime of life: a mature. well-developed creature just approaching middle age for its race. After that point, hit points usually decline. reaching as few as twice the minimum (newborn) hit points. Defeated monsters should only be wonh their full, listed XP value when at full adult hit points: you can reduce the XP value when a monster is too young or too old to have full hit points. 

Monster size also often varies by age. beginning at 10·25% of adult size and shrinking to 90% of adult size in old age. 

## **Environmental Variations** 

Monsters may easily be adapted to different environments. Under water. for example, play· ers would expect the usual predators fish. shark. octopus. etc.-but might be surprised to find underwater forms of birds, dragons, people, undead, and so fonh. ## **Undead Lieges and Pawns** 

Under cenain conditions. intelligent undead creatures can try to control other undead. The undead need not be a spellcastcr to control or her undead creatures. 

An undead creature being controlled by another is a _pawn._ An undead controlling one or more lesser undead is a _liege._ Skeletons and zombies can only be pawns, but any other type of undead can be either a liege or a pawn. Random encounters with undead may occasionally (10% chance) be with pawns controlled by a greater undead creature. 

A liege may control a number of undead whose tOtal Hit Dice arc less than or equal to _rwice_ rhe liege's Hit Dice. If an aucmpt by the liege ro control or her undead would cause rhc tO· 

tal ro exceed this amount, the aucmpr automati· cally fails. 

When a lich or other undead spellcastcr seeks ro conuol other undead, its _spellcurer level_ is used instead of its Hit Dice. Like a magic-user, a lich is far more powerful rhan its Hit Dice indicate. 

## **Procedure** 

If an undead uies to control a potential pawn, the target may have no more than half the Hit Dice of the liege. (This docs nor apply in cenain situations; sec below.) lf the subject is already controlled by any means. rhe undead auempt· ing control instantly recognizes this fact. It may still attempt control, but with a -4 penalty to the roll. 

If one undead tries to control another, find the Hit Dice of the would-be liege and potential pawn on the following table, and roll 2d6. If the number rolled is equal to or greater than the number given on the table, the attempt succeeds and the undead subject becomes the pawn of the conuollcr. A total of 2 or less (possible if the roll is penalized) always indicates failure. 

If the undead auempting conuol was once a spell-using character and can now usc spells as it did in life. a + 2 bonus applies ro all die rolls to control other undead. During melee. an auempt ro gain conuol is considered a combat action. 

If an undead creates another of the same type by slaying a living creature, the new undead is autOmatically a pawn of the sl:aycr if the slayer wants it to be. Spectres, vampires. wights, and wraiths arc the only undead with this ability. This may force the creator to release other exist· ing pawns; if so. the pawns with the highest Hit Dice arc released first. An undead would be wise to release a less-important pawn before the new pawn rises as an undead monster; that way. he can keep the pawns he wants. 

If an undead can call or summon others, those responding arc automatically its pawns unless the new Hit Dice total would exceed the limits given above, or unless the liege allows them to retain free will. 

## **Benefits to a Liege** 

A liege is telepathically linked ro its pawns and can sec and hear through t.hcm whenever it chooses. This communication is ar will and need nor be continuous. 

Conuol of a pawn is rotal, even to the point that it will obey suicidal orders: pawns obey without hesitation. The maximum range of conuol is 24 miles (one outdoor map hex) per Hit Die of the liege. 

If a pawn fails a morale check and flees from combat, the liege may srop the pawn and force ir back into melee. This can be the only action the liege takes during that melee round. The pawn will miss at least one full round of attacks. 

A liege can create a chain of control by instructing its pawns to become lieges too. For example, a spectre could control up to 12 wights, who could each control up to six skeletons. Direct communication and control docs not extend through a chain of control, but only to a liege's personal pawns. 

Any liege may coordinate the attacks of its pawns in a well-organized fashion. A liege at the top of a chain of control that consists of ten or more undead (counting the entire chain) may be considered the Leader of an undead army. ## **Immortals in the Game** 

s charaners reach higher experience levels. they will become aware of powers even mightier than they, powers beyond mom.l ken. The influence of these powers is deeply interwoven with the fabric of campaign _events._ and it becomes clear that these superior beings manipulate the world, perl-aps the entire multivcrse. according to their own desires. These beings are the Immortals.

lmmonals provide challenge for high level characters. Their sublle manipulations lead to campaign events. and the possibility of reaching this status provides characters with a new goal. An Immortal is a being who cannot die by earthly means. Immortals do not need food. drink, or air. They easily manipulate clements and magical energies while remaining almost lO· tally immune to their effects. 

The _Sphere of Energy_ is closely related to the element of fire. Its purpose is to create more energy and activity. Energy is highly active. dy· namic and excited. It seeks to alter and transform things, consuming matter, slowing time, and exciting thought to release more en· crgy. Highly temperamental , energy is also very creative. channeling magical energies and forming things from the ether. Energy rcprc· sents the Chaotic alignment (disorder and uniqueness) and favors the magic-user class. Energy is opposed to Thought's efforts to control it and seeks to transform Matter into energy to continue at its highest level despite the ravages of Time. 

## **Immortals and Spheres of Power** 

An Immortal's goals arc to gain personal power and to advance the influence of his Sphere. Immortals gain power through service to their Sphere: To increase the influence of one's Sphere is also to gain increased power from that Sphere. 

Once mortal heroes of legend, the Immortals gained powers and responsibilities beyond worldly concerns. Now Immortals, they subtly manipulate the events of the multivcrse to advance their Spheres of Power. Their maneuverings create challenges and epic sagas to test the worth of mortals while furthering the lmmor· tals' own mysterious goals. 

The paths of mortals and Immortals cross when service to a Sphere requires Immortals to intervene on the various planes of existence. Immortals have entered the lore and legends of the world through these chance encounters. 

The _Sphere of Time_ is closely related to the element of water. Its purpose is to promote change in all things and to ma.intain the flow of time. Time is everywhere. ebbing and flowing, recycling the lessons of the past to remind the present. It is a creative. shaping force causing change through aging and rebinh. Time repre· sents the Neutral alignment (seeking change. but also stability through the ages) and favors the cleric and druid classes. Time is opposed to Matter's effortS to withstand change, causes a loss of Energy through time, and teaches Thought the lessons of history. 

Each Immortal serves one Sphere of Power (described below), and the struggle for dominance between the Spheres of Power causes conflict in the campaign. 

The Prime Plane holds special interest for Immortals. It is the only place in which sentient humanoids occupy and manipulate an environment composed of all five Spheres. It is also the only place that reliably produces new Immortals. 

> Each Immortal has his own personal interests, often drawn from his experiences in life. One may be a patron of war, while another may be a patron of the arts. Each lmmortal promotes his own personal interests in the mortal world. 

Thus, many Immortals visit the Prime Plane with regularity. Once, in the distant past, Immortals lived in the Prime Plane and directly influenced the progress of the sentient races. They later departed, wisely. to preserve the plane's unique environment. 

Each Immortal is served by an order of clerics. The Immortal provides power (i.e., clerical spells) to his cleric followers, and also gives them guidance (often in the form of the clerical order's long-standing goals, but sometimes by directly or indirecdy manipulating the cleric into a specific quest or set of actions). 

The _Sphere of Thought_ is closely related to the element of air. Its purpose is to categorize all of existence and to make all other Spheres its tools. Thought is the very essence of the Immortals. It is realization , philosophy, and understanding. Thought seeks to analyze everything and can manipulate the other powers of the multiverse. Thought does not represent a single alignmeot, but is comprised of all alignments. It favors the thief and mystic classes. as the thief lives by his wits and cleverness and the mystic strives to live by philosophy and reason. Thought opposes the chaotic excesses of Energy and attempts ro rnanipulate the effects of Time ro create order and form in Matter. 

## **How the Immortals Interact With Mortals** 

Each Immortal draws strength from the numbers and devotion of his mortal followers (i.e .• the clerics and non-clerics who favor the Immortal and his goals). and so there arc also secondary struggles between Immonals who want to lure followers away from one another. 

Mortals on the Prime Plane are dealt with in· directly and through subversion. lmmonals do not commonly confront mortals directly. 

Immortals do not often appear to mortals in physical form , standing up before them and enjoining them to action. More commonly, an lmmona I will appear to one mortal in his dreams, or will inspire a cleric to a prophecy affecting the mortals. On rarer occasions. the Immortal will appear before a parry of mortals in his incorporcal form (see below). 

_Note:_ Not all clerics serve an Immortal, however. Some serve the less specific concepts of Law, Neutrality. and Chaos. while others serve great non-sentient forces such as Nature. 

The _Sphere of Enuopy_ or _Deach_ is not related to any element. Its purpose is the ultimate destruction of the multiverse. The four other Spheres of Power oppose Entropy but recognize its importance in the functioning of each of the other Spheres. Entropy is the weakening of the fabric of the multiverse. rot. weathering, and dissipation. It seeks to bring all things to a stop, causing oblivion. At the same time, Entropy it· self can not exist without the presence of the oth· cr powers, so it seeks first to subjugate before bringing about oblivion. Entropy docs not favor any specific class. Entropy seeks to destroy Mat· ter, dissipate Energy. cause Time to stagnate. and stop new Thought.
